exposure: subcutaneous infiltration of ropivacaine 0.5% 3 mg/kg alone
outcome: postoperative pain management (measured by VAS scores)
cohort: Participants were patients undergoing cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at Shahid Beheshti Hospital between 2022 and 2023.
finding: Subcutaneous infiltration of dexmedetomidine with ropivacaine improved postoperative pain management more effectively than ropivacaine alone, with the 2 mg/kg dose being more effective than the 1 mg/kg dose.
